title: Maximum Difference Between Increasing Elements
spaceBreakdown:
- int minSoFar: single scalar → O(1)
- int ans: single scalar → O(1)
- loop index j: single scalar → O(1)
- not counted: input vector nums
approach: For each index j, the best partner i < j is the one with the smallest nums[i], since nums[j] - nums[i] is maximized when nums[i] is minimized. So we scan left to right, maintaining the running minimum of elements seen so far. At each j, if nums[j] exceeds that minimum, we have a valid candidate difference; we track the maximum such difference. If no valid pair is ever found, we return -1.
hints: For a fixed right endpoint j, what property of the earlier index i makes nums[j] − nums[i] as large as possible? The array has up to 1000 elements.
Track the running minimum seen so far as you scan left to right. In [7,1,5,4], at j=2 the smallest value to the left is 1, giving candidate 5−1=4.

```
minSoFar = nums[0]
ans = -1
for j from 1 to n-1:
    if nums[j] > minSoFar:
        ans = max(ans, nums[j] - minSoFar)
    minSoFar = min(minSoFar, nums[j])
return ans
```

**All decreasing** - every element is smaller than all earlier ones, so no valid pair exists.
`Input: nums = [9,4,3,2]` → `Expected: -1`
⚠️ Bug: initializing ans to 0 instead of -1 → returns 0

**All equal** - strict inequality nums[i] < nums[j] never holds.
`Input: nums = [5,5,5]` → `Expected: -1`
⚠️ Bug: using `>=` instead of `>` in the comparison → returns 0

**Smallest valid input** - only two elements forming one valid pair.
`Input: nums = [1,2]` → `Expected: 1`
⚠️ Bug: starting the loop at j=0 so nums[0] is compared against itself → returns 0

**Best pair is not adjacent** - the optimal i is far from the optimal j.
`Input: nums = [1,5,2,10]` → `Expected: 9`
⚠️ Bug: only checking adjacent pairs (nums[j]-nums[j-1]) → returns 8

followUps.q: Return the actual indices i, j of the optimal pair instead of the difference.
followUps.a: Store the index of the running minimum alongside its value, updating both together. When a new best difference is found, record the current min-index and j. Time stays O(n), space stays O(1).

followUps.q: n can be up to 10^7 and the array arrives as a stream you can only read once.
followUps.a: The same single-pass running-minimum approach works unchanged since it only needs the current element and the running minimum. Time O(n), space O(1), no buffering required.

followUps.q: Find the maximum nums[i] − nums[j] with i < j (a decreasing pair) instead.
followUps.a: Mirror the logic: track the running maximum seen so far, and at each j compute maxSoFar − nums[j] when maxSoFar > nums[j]. Time O(n), space O(1).
